title: Auction-pipeline sequencing: announcement-to-settlement stage clock with forced primary-dealer warehousing

blindness_declaration.law: This document is authored before anyone measures anything for this lane. It declares a mechanism, a rule FAMILY and a representation identity. It contains no outcome numbers, no price/yield signal arithmetic, no conditioning of any price series on any state, and no measurement that the D2/I stages will run. Structural facts cited here are read from committed P0/P1/P2 artifacts only.

mechanism.narrative: Every auctioned security travels a fixed, pre-announced pipeline: announcement (terms known at once: cusip, securityType, securityTerm, auction date, issue date), then the auction itself, then issue/settlement, then seasoning. The pipeline has zero surprise content by construction: every date is published at the announcement. What is stage-dependent is the RISK the forced participant must carry. The primary dealer must pre-position hedges the day terms are announced, must bid at the auction, and must then warehouse the new security from settlement until it seasons into eligible indexes; the warehousing interval is a forced inventory carry whose length is set by the official calendar (issueDate relative to announcementDate), not chosen by the dealer. A decision instant therefore sits in an identifiable stage of a known event's pipeline, and the dealer's forced flow (pre-positioning versus post-settlement warehousing) differs by stage. This proposal conditions on the pipeline stage at each decision instant, derived by date arithmetic from the PIT census fields relative to the decision session. It differs from the dead policy-clock forms at the mechanism level: an FOMC-style clock conditions on an information RELEASE with unknown content; the auction pipeline carries no release surprise at all, only dated, pre-announced supply mechanics.

forced_participant.who: the primary dealer warehousing the newly issued security between settlement and index seasoning
forced_participant.why_forced: must bid at the auction and must carry the new security from its official issueDate; the carry length is set by the published calendar; balance-sheet and risk limits bind during the carry, so any adjustment flow the carry forces is timed by the pipeline, not by the dealer
forced_participant.late_participant: index and mandate-bound funds that can only make room for the seasoned security at index-add dates, after the dealer's carry window has already run

mechanism.information_source: official Treasury auction announcement calendar only (PIT census fields: announcementDate, auctionDate, issueDate, securityType, securityTerm, cusip); no prices, no yields, no survey or consensus data
mechanism.state_definition_symbolic: stage bucket s(t, e) = which of {announcement-era, auction-era, settlement-era} contains decision session t relative to event e's official dates, for the nearest eligible event(s); stage boundaries and the nearest-event rule are SYMBOLIC here and freeze at D2/S selection, never after

decision_rule_family: event-window position with state-conditioned direction by frozen sign convention; state = auction-pipeline stage bucket at the decision instant (announcement-era / auction-era / settlement-era), derived from PIT date arithmetic on the committed auction census; executed on the frozen ETP leg set; holding = fixed event window symbolic until D2/S; direction sign and all stage boundaries frozen at selection, never tuned after any measurement

event_mapping.law: PIT later-bound (P1 clock semantics, materialized at P2): the PIT instant is the end of the announced NY day; the same-day close is REFUSED; the decision session is the FIRST common-grid session STRICTLY AFTER the PIT instant; stage arithmetic additionally uses auctionDate and issueDate from the same census records, always compared to decision sessions that are STRICTLY AFTER the announcement PIT instant

event_mapping.state_derivation: at D2/I the stage state uses ONLY the census calendar fields by date arithmetic; never prices

decision_instant_law.law: V7 close+1: the EOD bar dated the previous common-grid session is first readable at the 16:00 NY close of each bookable session; no same-day reads; curve facts of calendar day d are PIT-available only from the first decision instant at/after the close+1 session of d

falsification_rule.statement: KILL if, at D2/I on the identical bookable grid and window under the identical frozen cost treatment, EITHER designated KILLER control (the shifted-calendar placebo or the pooled bare-pipeline-clock shadow) earns a strictly greater after-cost per-decision edge than the stage-conditioned ANCHOR arm. A placebo matching the anchor means the staging effect is calendar-structure-independent; a pooled shadow matching the anchor means the stage structure adds nothing over a generic event clock. Declared now, outcome-blind; measurable later from the committed arms alone.
